1 T he present contempt appeal under Section 19(1) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 is directed against the order dated 02.11.2022 passed by the Single Judge in contempt case (civil) No.415 of 2022, whereby the appellants herein have been awarded the punishment under Section 12 of Contempt of Court Act and sentenced to undergo six months' simple imprisonment.
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that after registering the suo moto contempt petition (civil) No.415 of 2022, a warrant has been issued against the present appellants.
Thereafter, they have appeared before the learned Single Bench on 21.03.2022 and they have been granted the benefit of bail.

Before the Court the appellants herein denied filing of the writ petition No.5723 of 2021 for medical termination of the pregnancy as well as abortion on incorrect averments, which persuaded this Court to pass the order, but looking to the discrepancy in the evidence given before the Trial Court where the offence under Section 363, 343, 376, 376(2)(N), 120-B, 376(d), 109, 366 of IPC and Section 5L/6, 5/17 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act was tried.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This Court in suo moto exercise of powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. directed the trial Court to re-examine the prosecutrix, her father and her brother.
In compliance thereof, the trial Court again recorded the statements of the appellants herein, wherein they all turned hostile.

In DNA test report as conducted in respect of the biological father of the aborted fetus produced before the Single Bench, it was found that the accused Sonu Parihar of Crime No.25 of 2021 was not the biological father of fetus,
therefore, the Single Judge vide order dated 30.08.2022 again directed to Superintendent of Police,
Datia for further the investigation and in compliance thereof, the status report was filed on 13.10.2022, wherein it came on record that the biological father of fetus is one Bhagwat Yadav, who is cousin brother of the prosecutrix and with respect to signature of appellant No.2 finding was also given that appellant No.2 i.e. father of the prosecutrix had not signed the Vakalatnama as well as the affidavit.
3. The Single Judge while dealing with the aforesaid issues, pointed out two contempt against the present appellants.

First contempt was with regard to filing of W.P. No.5723 of 2021 on false averments against appellants No.1 and 2 and second contempt was with respect of flouting of order dated 05.05.2022 and while making a false statement by the appellants.

4. The learned Single Bench in both contempt cases found the present appellants guilty and accordingly, vide impugned order dated 02.11.2022, present appellants were convicted under Section 12 of Contempt of Courts Act and sentenced to suffer six months simple imprisonment.
5. On considering the reasons assigned, we do not find any ground to interfere in the order passed by the learned Single Judge.
The reasons assigned by the learned Single Judge are appropriate.
We find no good ground to interfere in the matter.
6. Hence, the appeal is dismissed.
